requirement:
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments
supplying its tracked justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.

File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals;
function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
rationale:
The marked tests cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.justifications`.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

- **Show each `habeas:coverage` citation on the file root, a function or a method.**
  - `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs]` covers a root, a function (`fn[ordinary]`), a method (`impl[Worker]/fn[work]`) and an unexplained function (`fn[unexplained]`).
  - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[documentation_includes_non_rust_functions_methods_and_plain_file_roots]` covers Python, TypeScript and plain-file roots, functions and methods.
- **Exclude other attachments.**
  - In `notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs`, a citation on a nested module is asserted not to become a file exception. The nested child's docs are asserted not to appear.
  - `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citations_on_modules_and_citation_text_in_literals_do_not_create_explanations]` covers a module citation and citation text inside a string literal. It asserts that no proposal or explanation is shown.
- **Identify the source item and source location.**
  - The first test checks the item labels (`File root`, `fn[ordinary]`, `impl[Worker]/fn[work]`, `fn[unexplained]`).
  - It checks the exact `Source: code.rs:first–last` range for each entry.
  - It checks the `First source citation at line N` text for each entry.
  - It checks the workspace-relative file path.
- **Show fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments.**
  - The first test asserts root docs, a fenced root justification, function docs, function fenced commentary and method docs and commentary. It also asserts HTML escaping and that the output contains no raw `<unsafe>`.
  - `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[justification_can_come_from_docs_or_fenced_commentary_but_not_ordinary_comments]` tests docs alone, fenced commentary alone and ordinary comments alone. It checks the matching section headings.
  - The book test covers fenced commentary in non-Rust files.
- **Say so when no tracked justification is present.**
  - The ordinary-comment case in `justification_can_come_from_docs_or_fenced_commentary_but_not_ordinary_comments` asserts the message is present and the comment text is absent.
  - The `fn[unexplained]` entry in the first test asserts the message and that no "Rust doc comments" section appears.
  - The first test also asserts that the message appears exactly once. That shows it is not shown for justified entries.
- **Label proposals.**
  - The first test asserts exactly one "File-threshold exception proposal", on the root.
  - It asserts exactly three "Function exception proposal" entries, for the function, the method and the unexplained function.

**Gaps**

I found no unacknowledged gap. Every named case (root, function, method, justified, unjustified, docs, fenced commentary, non-doc comments) has a test with assertions that would catch a violation. The tests are correctly marked with `{test}` references to the subject.

One case is untested: a root citation with no justification. The requirement does not treat it differently from other entries, and the unjustified case is tested on a function.

I did not request implementation source.

Each listed file provides access to a file-notes view identifying its

:::{req} check.exceptions.anchor
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:coverage` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on a source file or explicitly declared function to propose a
> coverage exception. Explain in prose why the item's incomplete execution
> coverage is acceptable. Put the explanation in fenced citation commentary
> or Rust doc comments included in the source item's assessed input. An ordinary
> non-doc comment alone does not supply a tracked justification. The reason
> must be substantive; difficulty alone is not a justification.
> On a file's root item, the exception excuses only
> that file's 80% instrumented-line threshold, including absent measurement
> of its executable code. On an explicit function with a body, it excuses
> that function's recorded zero execution or absence from otherwise usable
> measurement, without excusing the file's threshold.
> The explanation must agree with the current source and any callers or
> configuration assumptions on which it relies. Only a current accepted
> independent assessment permits the exception. A file exception does not
> excuse unexecuted or not-measured functions in that file.
> The citation applies to its source item without conditional build matching
> and may remain when measured coverage satisfies the item's obligations.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference this built-in, inline or fenced using the standard
reference forms of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. The built-in MUST be
available in every project without a project requirement, site query, or
exception-specific configuration.
